day_shape: 76 items: Trump floats resumed Iran strikes after New Year if talks fail, ex-Mossad chief Barnea and Netanyahu press case for war, UK Treasury publishes Proliferation Financing risk assessment, Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks at wartime high, heavy IRGC/Basij Week messaging from Tehran.

threads.label: Trump strike threat and Israeli pressure
threads.summary: Trump said major strikes on Iran could resume after the New Year if negotiations fail and warned blockade runners would be sunk, as Israel reportedly seeks US coordination. Netanyahu called Iranian threats 'immediate', ex-Mossad chief David Barnea urged war 'as soon as conditions allow', and Iran International reported Washington is weighing a delay.

threads.label: Iranian defiance and missile-range claims
threads.summary: An Iranian lawmaker said Iran's missiles can now reach 4,500 km, doubling previously declared range, and Tehran warned against a US-backed Armenia transit corridor, invoking the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Minister Araghchi said enemies had failed to force 'unconditional surrender', while IRGC commander Vahidi vowed to respond to any aggression.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and regional maritime
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported shipping attacks around the Strait of Hormuz hit a wartime high in October with 22+ more in November per UKMTO, and the US Navy ordered 82 Lionfish undersea drones. CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper completed a weeklong tour of Israel, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, while Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon friction
threads.summary: IDF Arabic spokesman Avichay Adraee defended Israel's presence in south Lebanon after Lebanese objections to footage from Debel school, which the Lebanese PM said used schoolchildren for propaganda. IRIB claimed Israeli artillery shelled al-Ghondourieh and Wadi al-Hajir, sirens sounded in Even Menahem and Shtula, and Lavrov urged Israel to refrain from further clashes.

threads.label: UK proliferation-financing assessment
threads.summary: The Economic Secretary to the Treasury Lucy Rigby laid before Parliament the UK National Risk Assessment of Proliferation Financing, citing chemical, biological and nuclear weapons proliferation as a serious national security threat. Two parallel ministerial statements were published, naming proliferation financing as central to hostile-state capability.

threads.label: Basij Week messaging cycle
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB carried a sustained stream of Basij Week content, including IRGC commander Vahidi's message on martyrs' mothers, Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaii on basiji identity, and Basij head Taib accusing the US and Israel of misrepresenting the war's outcome. Khamenei's office released previously unpublished fiqh-lecture excerpts framing adversaries as 'the army of falsehood'.

threads.label: Iran domestic strains
threads.summary: Iran International reported around 150 poisonings and at least five deaths from adulterated alcohol fuelling criticism of the ban, and said land subsidence in southwestern Tehran has expanded roughly 20% in two years from groundwater extraction. Separately an underground feature film premiered at Tallinn without its banned makers, and a housing-crisis report described divorced couples still cohabiting.

events.title: 'Happy Ending' pushes the limits of Iran's underground cinema
events.summary: Happy Ending, Atena Mahmoudi's underground first feature about a young Tehran masseuse trying to leave Iran, premiered at Estonia's Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival without its makers, who are banned from leaving the country.
